answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a ocean as the anchor of the cost. A ember stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a wander holds...
